extractedWith: tools/extract/extract.ps1 -Batch p9-planning-skills -Manifest <scratch copy of allowlist.manifest.yaml with the p9-planning-skills batch> -Staging <scratch folder outside the repo> -Clean (scrub findings are expected before the rewrite; secret scan clean)
promotion: Each staged file was read as a reference only and rewritten with starter names and structure; "target" is the repo file it informed, "stagedTarget" the path in the staging folder. Content is a rewrite, so the repo file hash differs from stagedSha256. Left behind: the source-product tracker server, agent and credential handling, its roles, workflow and orientation section, and its comment markers.

origins.note: Rewritten for the starter: the plan goes to the tracked plans/<slug>.md, each phase names its feature spec and the starter skills that build it, acceptance criteria end in the starter test tiers; the plan template moved to PLAN-TEMPLATE.md.

Rewritten for the starter: the PRD goes to plans/<slug>-prd.md (not a gitignored agent folder), the tracker is optional and configured in plans/README.md (no hard-coded server, agent or credentials), the source-product orientation, roles and workflow were dropped; the PRD template moved to PRD-TEMPLATE.md.

Rewritten: the Remove/Simplify/Keep taxonomy kept with neutral examples; the source-product marker table replaced by starter markers (ADR, error codes, permission keys, analyzer ids); a differ section documents dialects, normalization and known limits.
Rewritten: workflow kept (ask, locate, classify, snapshot, verify, report); the verifier is now scripts/comment-diff.mjs; source-product examples and marker list replaced with starter ones.

Ported from Python to zero-dependency Node ESM and redesigned: per-language scanners (C# verbatim/interpolated/raw strings and char literals, script template holes and regex literals, HTML attributes and raw-text elements, T-SQL nested comments and bracket identifiers; SQL no longer treats // as a comment), literals compared byte for byte, line breaks kept significant, first-difference line report; unit tests in scripts/tests.
